$comment:
Irreversibility classification of the SDK's shipped operation surface, v0 — INV-7, SDK form.

WHY. INV-7 says no single trigger causes an irreversible transition. Its SDK-form obligation
is written against REACHABLE EFFECT, not local syntax: the question is what the SDK can
CAUSE, not what it contains. An earlier draft of this suite asserted 'the SDK contains no
destructive operations', reached by grepping for os.remove / rmtree / unlink / rmSync. That
found nothing and was reported as satisfaction. It was wrong: it had only asked about local
filesystem deletion and never about what the SDK could reach over the wire.

WHAT THE SURFACE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE. The generated gateway client ships in the wheel
(pyproject packages = [src/aegis_trust, src/aegis]) and is importable from an installed
aegis-trust. Across its whole operation set exactly one operation declares irreversibility
in its own docstring: destroy_capsule, 'Irreversibly destroy a capsule', POST
/capsules/{id}/destroy.

THE CONTRAST THAT MATTERS. Capsule RECALL is a deliberate two-step flow — recall/request
then recall/confirm — so it cannot fire from one call. Capsule DESTROY, the one operation
that cannot be undone, takes a single call with no confirmation step and no opt-in gate.
The two-step pattern this codebase already knows how to build is applied to the reversible
operation and not to the irreversible one. That is D8's shape restated at the SDK layer:
the default sits on the destructive side and nothing observes it.

WHAT THIS FILE ENFORCES (python/tests/test_irreversible_ops.py, node/tests/irreversibleOps.test.ts):
  1. Every shipped operation is classified. A new one fails CI until someone decides.
  2. Any operation whose docstring declares irreversibility must be classified irreversible,
     so the classification cannot drift from what the generator emitted.
  3. No irreversible operation is re-exported from the top-level public API. True today;
     asserting it stops it silently becoming false.
  4. The set of SINGLE-CALL UNGATED irreversible operations is pinned. It may shrink without
     ceremony. It cannot grow without this test failing.

HONEST STATE. ungated_single_call is non-empty. This file does not fix that — fixing it means
changing a shipped surface, which is a product decision, not a test change. What it does is
make the count machine-visible and prevent a second one appearing unnoticed.

classes.irreversible: Reaches a Core-side transition that cannot be undone (AO-004 Wiped / Destroyed).
classes.two_step: Part of a deliberate multi-call flow; no single call completes the effect.
classes.reversible: Effect can be undone, or the operation is a read/query.

destroy_capsule.reachable_from: an installed aegis-trust, by importing the generated client module directly
destroy_capsule.note: One call from the shipped package reaches an irreversible transition FOR A CALLER HOLDING ADMIN. An unprivileged caller importing the generated client gets 403, so the earlier reading — that any installed aegis-trust reaches destruction — overstated it. What remains, and what INV-7 is about, is that no second step stands between one Admin call and an irreversible effect. Remediation (a gate, an explicit opt-in, or removal) narrows a shipped API surface and is an owner decision, not an SDK one.
destroy_capsule.server_side_authorization: Authenticated (Extension<AuthContext>) + Role::Admin via can_execute_destructive(); 403 Forbidden otherwise, re-checked inside handle_trigger_destroy_pub as declared defence-in-depth. Measured in aegis-boundary-core (rest.rs route/handler) by the Core implementer and REPORTED HERE, not verified from this repository — nothing in aegis-trust CI can see that code, so this is attribution, not measurement.
destroy_capsule.why_not_recorded_as_gate: Because `gate` is load-bearing: test_irreversible_ops.py counts an entry with a truthy `gate` or `confirmation_step` as gated and removes it from the exposed set. Authorization is not the opt-in INV-7 requires — its statement is 'no single call causes an irreversible transition; irreversible destruction requires explicit opt-in', and an Admin who mistypes a capsule id still destroys it in one call. Writing a true fact into that field would have closed the hole in the guard's view without closing it.

node_asymmetry.state: node/src has no generated gateway client and no destroy or wipe surface.
node_asymmetry.consequence: With respect to INV-7 the two SDKs are not the same product. Declared here so the asymmetry is visible rather than discovered later.
node_asymmetry.enforced_by: node/tests/irreversibleOps.test.ts asserts the Node source stays free of an irreversible surface; if one is added, that test fails and this entry must be rewritten.
